graph.summary: Methotrexate → 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleotide formyltransferase/IMP cyclohydrolase → Adenosine → Adenosine receptor A2a → Rheumatoid Arthritis

evidence.snippet: Methotrexate (MTX), a synthetic folate analog, is a tight-binding inhibitor of dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), a key enzyme for the biosynthesis of purines, thymidylate, and several amino acids.

paper.title: The effects of methotrexate on Drosophila development, female fecundity, and gene expression.
paper.journal: Toxicological sciences : an official journal of the Society of Toxicology

evidence.snippet: The polyglutamated derivatives of methotrexate are potent inhibitors of various enzymes, including dihydrofolate reductase and 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleotide transformylase.

paper.title: Methotrexate in rheumatoid arthritis. An update.

evidence.snippet: intracellular MTX polyglutamates inhibit AICAR transformylase (ATIC) activity and thereby promote adenosine release

paper.title: Fibroblasts from methotrexate-sensitive mice accumulate methotrexate polyglutamates but those from methotrexate-resistant mice do not.

evidence.snippet: ATIC activity was inhibited following MTX treatment in DF from BALBc mice
evidence.explanation: ATIC normally consumes AICAR in purine synthesis; its inhibition leads to AICAR accumulation and downstream adenosine release. The snippet confirms ATIC inhibition by MTX treatment; increased adenosine production was also demonstrated in the same paper.

paper.title: Fibroblasts from methotrexate-sensitive mice accumulate methotrexate polyglutamates but those from methotrexate-resistant mice do not.

evidence.snippet: The blockade of purine nucleotide biosynthesis by MTX at the AICA ribonucleotide transformylase-catalyzed step may be related to the efficacy of MTX, and this blockade is effectively relieved by folinic acid, but not by folic acid, supplementation.
evidence.explanation: ATIC inhibition (blockade at AICA ribonucleotide transformylase step) leads to AICAR accumulation and adenosine release; this sentence describes the blockade and its clinical significance.

paper.title: The effect of folic acid and folinic acid supplements on purine metabolism in methotrexate-treated rheumatoid arthritis.

evidence.snippet: adenosine, acting at one or more of its receptors, mediates the antiinflammatory effects of methotrexate in animal models of both acute and chronic inflammation

paper.title: Adenosine A2A or A3 receptors are required for inhibition of inflammation by methotrexate and its analog MX-68.

evidence.snippet: these results provide strong evidence that adenosine, acting at either or both of these receptors, mediates the antiinflammatory effects of methotrexate and its analog MX-68

paper.title: Adenosine A2A or A3 receptors are required for inhibition of inflammation by methotrexate and its analog MX-68.
